page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core and memory performance. The c9g.8xlarge achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench tests, software compilation with Clang, and text processing. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top tier. Memory performance is notable, with a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong cached read-only memory bandwidth. Database operations and static web serving throughput are exceptionally high. However, large block uncached memory read and write speeds, along with single-core stress-ng performance, fall into the average range.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical cores, the c9g.8xlarge offers high resource density and compute efficiency for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is highly suited for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and text processing. The instance also handles medium-scale language model inference and multi-threaded decompression efficiently, making it a viable choice for containerized microservices, CI/CD pipelines, and compute-heavy web applications.
